name: Brood vent
description:
The thing that follows you and pushes out grubs — an orifice, and now a body with an orifice in it rather than a plate with a hole through it. What was here was three hexagons inside each other, which is a pucker the way a bolt head is one: the geometry never stopped being the shell plate it was cut from and only the colours had moved, so nothing about it could be animated except turning the middle one, and a cut cell revolving inside a plate that does not is a mechanism's motion.

This is built out from the closure instead. A mound of skin — a forty-point outline off three harmonics, so no run of the edge repeats, lit along the top and shaded under — with a socket sunk into it, the everted flesh standing in that socket, ten folds swirling out of the closure across the flesh and on over the skin, and the closure itself: a soft eight-point star of `$soil.dark` inside a ring of `$blood.dark2` that always opens wider than the star does, so the wet reads as a rim and never as a face. The gut the grubs come out of hangs under all of it, drawn in the same skin shaded rather than in a darker colour, because a darker mass there reads as a second object.

Nothing about it is centred or even. The opening sits up and left of the mound's middle; the folds are unevenly spaced, unevenly long and unevenly wide, and they all swirl the same way round, because a ring of straight wedges at even angles is a parasol. A vent centred in its own mound is a badge, and this is meant to be part of something.

The reds are still held back on purpose: a saturated `$blood` face reads as an alarm on a screen where red means something is wrong, and this thing is yours. The ramp steps `$rust.light2` skin → `$ember.dark` flesh → `$blood.dark2` → `$soil.dark`, and what it is built to protect is the one thing that has to survive eighteen pixels: dark centre inside light ring. The folds are what keep that from reading as an iris: struck at `$soil@0.55` and running in to the closure, they stripe the flesh instead of leaving a clean bright disc round a dark dot, which is most of the difference between a pucker and an eye. Against the field's floor `scripts/readability.ts` reads 2.50 where the old plate read 2.03 — exactly the line this app draws under a body, and where it stays, held there by the two things the drawing will not give up: a hair of `$ink` all the way round and a centre that has to be a hole.

Two clips, because it does two things. `hum` is the idle: the pucker works round rather than all at once — each fold on its own beat of the same two seconds — the gut fills and settles, and the closure breathes against it. `lay` is one grub leaving, and the consumer plays it once per grub: it draws in, throws the closure wide, the pale bead crests the lip and is gone, the clench comes down behind it, and the next one rises in the throat while the folds settle. `meta.layCue` 0.33 is the contract that goes with it — the share of the clip at which the vent is widest and the bead leaves, so the game can release the real grub (`ss.proj.chip`) on that frame instead of on the frame the strain starts. The bead is the grub and the grub is the bead; they are never both on screen.

It does not spin and it no longer travels: the weapon that carries this stopped walking it round the player, so every motion in the document is the body's own.

hum.description: a body idling: the pucker works round, the gut fills and settles

lay.description: one grub out — draw in, throw wide, the grub over the lip, the clench behind it, the next one rising
